title: Two-column sorting sheet
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Forces, magnets and light (Mighty Metals and Why Do Cat's Eyes Glow at Night?)
source: Seeded from science/y3 lesson 11 (Two-column sorting sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 11: Magnetic and non-magnetic materials. To understand that only some materials are magnetic

blocks.title: Sort into: Magnetic / Non-magnetic
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Magnetic, Non-magnetic.
blocks.answer: Magnetic: steel paper clip; iron nail; steel scissors blade; fridge door. Non-magnetic: plastic ruler; wooden spoon; rubber; glass jar

questions.model: Ask: is it made of iron or steel? Wood is not. So the magnet will not pull it. It is non-magnetic.

questions.a: Yes, most steel is magnetic because it contains iron.

questions.q: Finish: 'Magnetic objects are usually made of ...'
Core: Test 8 objects at home with a fridge magnet. Sort them in a two-column table: magnetic and non-magnetic.
questions.a: Pupils' own; steel and iron objects are magnetic, plastic, wood, glass and fabric are not.
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: hold the magnet close to a key, a sock and a tin. Write each in the right column.

questions.q: Extend: Did any results surprise you? Write one.
questions.a: For example: foil is a metal but was not magnetic.

questions.q: Stretch: Write a rule that fits all your results.
questions.a: For example: things made of iron or steel are magnetic; other materials are not.

questions.q: Big question: what makes something stick to a magnet?
questions.a: It is made of a magnetic material such as iron or steel.
